title: A Love Stronger Than Heaven or Hell
source: Author-supplied manuscript: Part Seven Michael; Part Eight Explanation; Part Nine Understanding
note: Narration split into readable sections; spoken dialogue is preserved as supplied. Portrait expressions and curated images are presentation metadata; no combat was invented for these chapters.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Michael stood in his ivory tower, facing one panel of the large encirclement of windows surrounding his office. He heard Uriel enter through the sole door behind him.

events.speaker: MICHAEL
events.text: Yes, Uriel?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Michael asked, not taking his eyes off the golden bridges below, connecting the sea of clouded islands.

events.speaker: URIEL
events.text: My sources have confirmed that Asmodeus and Haniel both survived. Shall I send aid?

events.speaker: MICHAEL
events.text: No,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: There was silence.

events.speaker: URIEL
events.text: Are you certain of that? Haniel is likely weak, and she is our sister.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Flecks of white flame glimmered in and out of existence around him. Uriel was the most pragmatic of their siblings, the calmest and most calculated, which was precisely why they were not fit for a leadership position. Leadership was for one with passion, someone with a burning inferno in their heart and molten lead flowing through their veins.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: As God’s wrath, that was Michael’s natural role.

events.speaker: MICHAEL
events.text: I already have things well in hand, Uriel.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: From beneath Uriel’s many cloaks, Michael saw a curious look full of doubt.

events.speaker: URIEL
events.text: Perhaps I should inform Father,

events.speaker: MICHAEL
events.text: We shouldn

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: t bother Father with such nonsense, lest we all suffer the consequences. I have this under control,” Michael said.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He felt the blade at his side grow hot within its sheath, burning to unleash its fury.

events.speaker: URIEL
events.text: Very well. However, I would rather not see Haniel go the way of our brother. It would be a shame for our seven to become five.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Uriel exited the room without another word.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Michael’s windows cracked as Uriel left, leaving him unsure if it was a release of his own pent-up rage or a threat from Uriel. He walked to his chair, a comfortable wooden armchair, and sat facing the small pedestal with a soft blue ball of glass resting upon it.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: His first attempt had failed.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: His attempt to help his sister, a delicate thing who could not even speak for herself.

events.speaker: MICHAEL
events.text: The bear almost worked,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Had Haniel not been so soft, his plan would have worked. He would not forget such treason, yet he would forgive her, just as their Father had taught.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus sat at Alric’s oaken table. It wasn’t as well built as his furniture in Hell, though compared to his drying rack, it might as well have been made for royalty. Looking to Haniel, he saw her discomfort.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She hadn’t seemed content since the alley incident, even though he let them linger until the boy’s parents arrived and took him home safe and sound, minus the broken arm. That child deserved much worse than what he got.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Had it been his choice, had he known it wouldn’t upset Haniel, he likely would have ripped the thug’s throat out and called it even.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: You gonna get over this soon?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He didn’t receive hand signs in the traditional sense, but rather a crude gesture.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Didn

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: I have siblings,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: she signed in response. Her signs were quick and sloppy from agitation, so reading them was a hassle.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Why are you even mad? Kid was gonna cut you up. He deserved worse if you ask me,

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Aye, the boy did have a broken bone or two coming. That group

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: s been acting up for a while now. Hopefully you knocked some sense into them,” Alric said, setting cups in front of them along with a plate of pastries.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Yet I suspect your lass is less angry about the extremes you went through and more angry you did it when you already had him at your mercy. She seems like the good-natured sort,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus could see that Alric was a man who had worked his whole life, and looking to Haniel’s gentle nodding, he saw that Alric was correct.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: It amazed Asmodeus how vicious Haniel could be in battle, yet outside of it, without the orders of Heaven, she was kind and gentle, though perhaps too much so.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: I know you aren

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: And neither of you should be. My wife and I don

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus eyed the room around them. Things like books he doubted Alric would read, sappy romantic things, and toys were spread through the house, indicating children of a variety of ages.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Can

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: t believe I’m in the doghouse when I’m not even getting any,” Asmodeus said with a sigh.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Watch your mouth. Children could be around,

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Yeah, because young people don

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel didn’t respond with signs, but rather gave him a stern look.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Fine, damn. I swear I

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The room was quiet as Haniel and Alric stared blankly at him.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Well… regardless… my three children are off doing their schooling,

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Might I ask what brings such interesting, not-human folks to my town?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel flinched and Asmodeus prepared himself for violence.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: How did you know?

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: She has wings and white hair… and you have a tail and red eyes…

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus looked behind him to his own tail, then noticed Haniel had also glanced at his tail.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Pervert!

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel made a quick, semi-panicked motion before looking indignantly in his direction, then looking to Alric for support. Asmodeus was pleased with the results of his teasing.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: m a demon and she’s an angel. We fought, and now we’re weakened and trying to survive. We live a few miles east of here,” Asmodeus said bluntly.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Mighty exciting people you are indeed,

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Why aren

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: A couple weeks ago, I saw blue and red lightning in the clouds. Then today I saw a man with a tail and a woman who certainly looks the part of an angel. The dots aren

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Did you get what ya came here for?

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Yeah, herbs to help Haniel. She was weakened further after saving my ungrateful ass from a bear,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus said, tapping his finger against the table.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I see. Is there anything I can do to help you?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric’s gaze moved to Haniel, and Asmodeus’s followed. She was pointing at the very table they were sitting at.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: My table? I built this when I married my wife, so unfortunately I can

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: t part with it,” Alric said, receiving a shake of Haniel’s head in response.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric’s eyes widened with the gleam of an understanding that still eluded Asmodeus.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: You want to learn carpentry?

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Makes sense. My drying rack turned out poorly,

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: You can hunt, and I will make what we need,

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: m a smith and carpenter by trade, so I can certainly teach ya,” Alric said.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: You seem like a lady who

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: And I

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: ll even get you a book on gardening and some equipment for it,” Alric said with a smile.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel sat outside their cave. Alric told them he would visit to get Asmodeus started on gardening and to teach her some woodworking. A few hours after sunrise, a small wooden wagon neared. Alric was walking next to it, and the wagon was being pulled by a pair of boys, one she recognized and one she did not.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric stopped in the clearing by their cave, motioning to the boys: the teenage thug from before and a younger boy in the waning years of his childhood.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I brought aid,

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Get over here, boys,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric said, motioning them over.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: That

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Joren, do you have something to say to these fine people?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: It wasn’t a request from Alric, but a demand.

events.speaker: JOREN
events.text: I

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Is that enough?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The pregnant pause seemed to expand infinitely.

events.speaker: JOREN
events.text: No,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Joren said, a mix of fear, embarrassment, and sadness coloring his aura.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: He

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: s a foolish brat, but his family are farmers, so he can show ya the ropes of farming,” Alric said, annoyance coloring Asmodeus’s aura.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: If you still need to get in a few whacks after he

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Fine,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The other boy walked up to them and bowed politely.

events.speaker: TOREN
events.text: My name is Toren,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The child was adorable, but she did not know what to convey. She had never been a child and didn’t know how to interact with them. Would waving be enough, or would a pat on the head be in order? Or would such a familiar touch be rude or seen as condescending?

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Toren will also help you get some farming started. It will take several days, but they are strong lads,

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: And what will you be doing then?

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I brought my extra tools and some lumber, so I will be teaching the lady woodworking,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The explanation seemed enough for Asmodeus, and he left with the boys for his lesson on living alongside nature.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I like that one. He

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel nodded, watching the boy whose arm was in a sling pull buckets from the wagon—an arm Asmodeus had damaged.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: He

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: I took my fair share of punishment when I was a young man. They heal quickly and hopefully learn an important lesson,

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: He still did it,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric thought for a moment.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Aye, he did. My wife and I aren

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: t perfect either. We do things all the time that the other one doesn’t like, but do you know what helps with that?” Alric asked.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel shook her head. There was no way she could know about a woman she had never seen before.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: We understand why each other does the things we do, even if we don

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: As a father, I don

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: t approve of such an action, but as a man, I understand the truth. He just wanted to protect you. Can’t fault him for that,” Alric said with a shrug as they watched the three work upon the land from afar, Joren explaining various things and Asmodeus listening and nodding.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: It

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel opened her mouth to correct, to argue, but Alric spoke once more.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Even if you are not husband and wife, it is clear that there is fondness between the two of you. Regardless of what form that takes, it is precious.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel stared at a patch of earth. She had to go back to heaven, had to see Azriel and the others, yet Alric was correct. She was beginning to care for this hellspawn, and that was sinful.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A memory crossed her mind, a single image: her forsaken brother wrapped in chains as he was cast to the land below. His face had been twisted into something ugly, a face of anger and fear, yelling and crying. She didn’t understand it then, but perhaps she was beginning the journey to understanding such things.

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: What

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Thinking about my brothers, one younger and one older,

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: Mind telling me about them?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Alric asked, taking some wood from the wagon.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: One was a rebel, and the other is the kindest soul I have ever met,

events.speaker: ALRIC
events.text: It sounds like you love them very much,

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She did love them. She loved all her siblings, even the one she was told not to, because to love was simply her nature.
